summary: Otto Blau worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under August Friedrich Pott (~1848–1851) at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1848) and at Leipzig University (~1850–1852).

Otto Fischer specialized in sinology and history/archaeology, studying at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen. He was director of Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920), head of Kunstmuseum Basel (1927), and associate professor of art history at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

Otto Franke was a sinologist and indologist who studied at Freiburg, Göttingen, and under Wilhelm Grube. He held chairs at the Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut and University of Hamburg (1910–1923) and was professor of sinology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1923–1931).

Otto Höfler worked in linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology, studying at Vienna, Lund, and Kiel under Rudolf Much. He held posts at Uppsala, Lund, Kiel (1935), Munich (1938–1945, 1954), and the University of Vienna (1957–1971).

Otto Jahn was a scholar of history/archaeology and related fields who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held positions at Kiel (~1839–1842), Greifswald (~1842–1847), Leipzig (~1847–1851), and the University of Bonn (~1855–1869).

Otto Maenchen-Helfen was a scholar of sinology, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig under August Conrady, and held posts at the Marx-Engels-Lenin Institute (1927–1929), Mills College (1939–1947), and UC Berkeley (1947–1962).

Otto Neugebauer worked in history/archaeology, studying at Graz, Munich, Copenhagen, and Göttingen under Boris Turayev. He held posts at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University as professor of the history of mathematics (1939–1969), and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Otto Rosenberg specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Bonn under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, Sergey Oldenburg, Hermann Jacobi, and Rudolf Lange, and served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University (1911–1919).

Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at Charles University under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. He spent his academic career at Charles University, serving as Privatdozent in 1922 and ordinary professor of Indian philology and archaeology from 1930 to 1939.

Otto Strauß specialized in Indology and philosophy, studying at Berlin, Munich, and Kiel under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He served as professor at the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), Kiel (1920), and the University of Breslau (1928–1935).

Otto von Böhtlingk worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Saint Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn under Franz Bopp and Christian Lassen. He served at the Russian Academy of Sciences (1842–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).
Owen Flanagan is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Fordham University and Boston University, and was appointed Professor of Philosophy at Duke University around 1996.

P. A. Payutto is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1958–1962). He served there as Associate Dean (~1964–1974) and was named Tipitaka Acharaya at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1995.

P. D. Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Peradeniya, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under David J. Kalupahana and Eliot Deutsch, and served as head of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Peradeniya (1997–2004).

P. K. Mukhopadhyay is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and served as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).
P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indologist who studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bishop Heber College and the University of Madras. He served at Bishop Heber College, Rajah's College, and Annamalai University as Sanskrit department head (1942–1947).
Padma Subrahmanyam is a scholar in Indology. She studied at Ethiraj College for Women, Stella Maris College, and Annamalai University (~1970–1979) under research supervisor T. N. Ramachandran.
Padmanabh S. Jaini was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Professor (attested 1977–1990, 2002) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2016) at the University of California, Berkeley.

Palden Sherab was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche. He served as chair of the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1984).
